thread.document:
Our Website: https://reateam2.vercel.app/

Group Members: Dagny Streit, Justin Li, Hanna Roed, Nils Svelte

This project produced a reproducible pipeline that collects, cleans, and presents EECS 182 extra credit participation posts in a structured and searchable format. The main challenge was obtaining the discussion data in a reliable way, since Ed does not provide a built-in export feature. Solving this problem made it possible to organize student contributions in a form that is easy to browse, analyze, and revisit.

To collect the data, we wrote a Python script that uses Ed’s API to iterate through all discussion threads and identify posts titled “Special Participation A.” For each matching post, the script extracts the cleaned title, author name, full text, and a link to the original discussion. The results are saved into a CSV file, forming the base dataset used for the website and further analysis. During development, we encountered inconsistent API responses, which required debugging and adding error checks to ensure stable data collection.

After generating the initial dataset, we wrote a second script to extract structured information from post titles, such as the model used and the homework number. Because students used many different title formats, the script relied on flexible pattern matching. Most entries were parsed correctly, and a small number of remaining errors were fixed manually to ensure accuracy.

Cursor and ChatGPT was used throughout the project to help generate code, debug errors, and improve parsing logic. The final workflow reflects several iterations of testing and refinement based on real data. Once the dataset was complete, we built a website using Cursor and deployed it on Vercel. The site allows users to search posts by author, model, or content, sort posts by homework or model, and view automated summaries that highlight trends across submissions. Together, the pipeline and website make student work easier to explore and give lasting visibility to ideas shared throughout the semester

*This summary was also AI generated to match the “vibe coding” theme
